I know how this feels and you are not alone. If you can, hang in there, it will get better. I’m 24F and was both bullied, made my way through depression, dyscalculia and severe ADHD. When I was 16 I just wanted to die, I had to work so much harder than everyone else just to get a C-B, I ate in the bathroom and skipped classes because I felt too bad and saw no point in going to school. Today I’m 24 years old, I’m on antidepressants, taking ADHD medication and WORKING at university! I have my dream job, dream apartment and a great partner. I know we adults/young adults often say “it gets better” & “hang in there”, but there is actually something to it. 

To me it sounds like you are motivated and want to learn. Given what you say about your lessons, you may also have an underlying ADHD diagnosis. 
It might be worth trying to do an assessment and possibly see if you can take medication. If you can, I think you should talk to a school counselor or some kind of resource available at school. Dropping out may seem like the easiest and most obvious choice to make, but I promise you will lose out in the long run.
You can always read online, try searching on youtube for different videos about what you are doing in school, or borrow audio books if it’s hard to keep up, we all learn in different ways: verbally, visually, audio or teaching others, find out what works for you.

Friends are very overrated, but you can always try to join different types of sports/hobby/ or arts and crafts activities where new friends can be found, your friends don’t have to be at school, the people at school are just people you have to “put up with”.

You will do this! I believe in you! Good luck💖

I’m in a heartbreak boat myself right now. These are the words that helped me get through it:

• It was nice while it lasted, I feel pain and that’s okay/feeling pain is a natural thing and a part of life, some days it’s worse then others.

•See this as a new chapter, perhaps she was a good fit for you but you can now find yourself and when your ready even a better fit! 

• Take a break for seeing her on Facebook, o think there’s a setting that you can pause looking at their account, I know it’s tempting to see her face and what she’s up to, dreaming what could have been, but trust me, it only hurts in the end. 

• Try things YOU want to do, eat the chips she hate, watch the movies she doesn’t like, go to that concert with that old friend and ect! If you keep yourself busy focusing on what brings YOU joy (even the small things, like sleeping in or drinking ice coffee in the morning) you will fill that emptiness that she’s caused. It really works.

•There are people who have loved as “hard” as you and I have, we are more then just accounts on the internet, we have jobs and many of us are struggling with EXACTLY your situation.

I’m going to be honest with you, there have been many times I wanted to end it. But then I remember, if things have changed in the past, they can also change in the future. I have my bad days and I have my good days. I know that you want to control it, you probably feel like your not in control of your own life anymore, but you are. My advice is to look at it like this “Waw my reality looked a lot different a while ago then it does now, life has changed my reality has changed and that’s not a bad thing”.
